The Ghana Developing Communities Association (GDCA) has called for greater transparency in the allocation and release of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), alongside stronger accountability mechanisms to ensure the resources deliver the intended development outcomes.
Executive Director of GDCA, Philip Gmabi, says delays in releasing funds and limited flexibility in their utilisation can undermine the ability of district assemblies to implement projects and respond to the needs of their communities.
He made the call during a GDCA-JoyNews national dialogue on a study of DACF allocation equity and guideline implementation in Ghana (2020–2025).
Speaking under the theme From Allocation to Receipt: Making the DACF Work for Poorer Districts, Mr Gmabi said the effectiveness of the Fund depended not only on how allocations were determined but also on the processes through which the money reached assemblies and was utilised.
He noted that unpredictable releases affected development planning, created uncertainty for contractors and service providers, and delayed improvements expected by communities.
“When releases are delayed or uncertain, assemblies struggle to plan and carry out projects, contractors and service providers face uncertainties, and communities wait longer for improvements,” he said.
Mr Gmabi called for predictable release schedules, clear communication and transparent reporting to enable assemblies to plan with confidence and allow citizens to track public funds.
He also advocated greater flexibility in the use of the Fund, arguing that assemblies should have reasonable discretion to direct resources towards their specific development priorities.
He cautioned, however, that such flexibility must be accompanied by proper financial management, transparent decision-making, public participation and accountability.
He said citizens must be able to follow the use of the DACF from the point of allocation to the delivery of projects and services to determine whether the resources are producing the intended results.
Mr Gmabi urged stakeholders at the dialogue to identify practical reforms that would strengthen the entire funding process and improve the responsiveness of the Fund to local development needs.
The study, titled Comprehensive Study on DACF Allocation Equity and Guideline Implementation in Ghana (2020–2025), was commissioned by GDCA under its Empowerment for Life (E4L) Programme.
Authored by Professor Abdul-Gafaru Abdulai and Dr Kwadwo Opoku of the University of Ghana, the study examines DACF allocations, releases and utilisation between 2020 and 2025, with particular attention to ten E4L focus districts.
It also assesses the 2025 DACF Use Guidelines against the 2026–2029 Medium-Term Development Plans of six of the focus districts.
